answer: Agent vaults can cap how many identities any single operator may register, tying each one to a distinct hardware enclave key and a modest stake that slashes on misbehavior. A public registry publishes reputation peaks, so the zenith of an honest agent is visible to counterparties, while fresh identities start at zero and earn standing only through attested work. A quiet whisper of doubt then attaches automatically to bulk-created lookalike accounts: sybils become expensive, slow, and easy to spot against the established registry.
